title: Cross-talk between Myocardial Metabolism and Other Organs Investigated by Magnetic Resonance Spectroscopy
summary:
The heart needs a constant supply of energy to pump blood throughout the body. How it produces this energy also depends on how other organs and the body as a whole regulate metabolism. In diseases such as diabetes, this interaction can be disrupted and affect heart health.

Magnetic resonance spectroscopy (MRS) allows us to study metabolic processes in the heart and other organs without taking tissue samples. New techniques even enable us to track how certain substances are processed in the body. Our goal is to better understand how the heart and metabolism interact and how this relationship changes in cardiovascular diseases and diabetes.

interventions.name:
Performance of MRS sequences (¹H, ²H, ¹³C, and ³¹P) on clinical 3T and ultra-high-field 7T MRI scanners, outside routine clinical practice.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
•	Healthy subjects
•	Diabetes no exclusion criterion
Exclusion criteria:
•	Contraindications to MRI (Implants, pregnancy)
•	Missing informed consent
